text: Small-world networks are characterized by high clustering coefficients combined with long average shortest path lengths relative to a random graph of the same size.
explanation: This statement is false: small-world networks combine high clustering with a SHORT average path length relative to random graphs, not a long one. That combination -- high local clustering plus efficient global connectivity -- is the defining feature of the Watts-Strogatz small-world model, and most biological networks display this property.
